facts.incident.description: I was lifting a heavy cast-iron casserole pot down from the shelf above the cooktop and it slipped out of my hands onto the cooktop. The ceramic glass top shattered in a star pattern from the front left cooking zone right across the top.
facts.incident.cause: A cast-iron pot dropped onto the cooktop by accident
facts.loss.description: Built-in 60 cm ceramic glass cooktop shattered across the whole top; it cannot be used
facts.mitigation.emergency_action: Turned the cooktop off at its wall isolation switch and left it off; cooking with the microwave and the barbecue for now
facts.policyholder.name: Charlotte Chenmoor
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the smashed cooktop with the pot next to it. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: The quote from Harakeke By Appliances has two pages; I only scanned the first page. I can find the second page later.
facts.if_asked_about_quote_total: i dont know, the total is on the second page and i havent found it yet
facts.if_asked_about_cooktop_age: it was here when we bought the house in 2021, i think its about 7 years old

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo looking down at a built-in black ceramic glass cooktop set into a light oak kitchen benchtop. The black glass is shattered in a star-shaped web of cracks spreading from the front left cooking zone across the whole top, with small chips of glass missing at the impact point. A heavy dark red cast-iron casserole pot sits on the benchtop beside the cooktop. Warm evening kitchen downlights. The frame is a close crop of the cracked cooking zones and the benchtop edge around them.

design.notes: The two-page quote keeps only page 1 (header, dates and line items); page 2 with the totals is missing and page 1 still prints 'Page 1 of 2'.

triage.rationale: The appliance store's quote is missing its second page, so someone must chase it. Nobody is hurt, the cooktop is switched off and the home is habitable, so nothing is complex. Page 1 shows the line items but not the total, and the claimant does not know it, so whether the amount counts as known is left open. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

quote_before_loss.basis: The quote date is on the retained page 1: 21 September 2026, after the incident on 16 September 2026. The removed page 2 holds only the totals and terms.

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 July 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2021-07-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
